text: What if your competitor could read your trading agent's shopping list? With x402 today, they can. Every payment an agent makes is public.
Which feed it bought, how often, and when. That is alpha anyone can front-run.

text: Odds Desk is a research agent that buys Gemini prediction market signals for fractions of a cent, and pays privately. Let's run it.
The whale feed sits on an unvetted origin. The policy runs inside the x402 hook, so it is refused before anything is signed.

text: A batch of five credits costs one cent. That is above my auto-approve limit, so the agent asks me first.

It blinds five serials. Circle Gateway settles one gasless nanopayment on Arc, and the mint signs without ever seeing them. Then three paid requests. No transactions, and the seller only knows: anonymous.
Then it makes its call, from a volatility model that beat the naive read by twenty six percent on seven hundred thirty six settled Gemini contracts.
Blind credit is a new x402 scheme, built on the official interfaces. Next, we want to upstream it.
